stem: Upper inflorescences show more advanced glandular-trichome maturation than lower inflorescences on the same plant. What is the best assessment approach?
choices: Sample multiple representative canopy positions and compare their developmental and trichome observations before assigning a crop maturity state
Use the upper-canopy samples because stronger light exposure makes those flowers the most reliable indicator of whole-plant harvest readiness
Average the upper and lower observations into one percentage without retaining canopy position because location becomes irrelevant after sampling
Use the planned harvest date to decide which canopy sample should be considered representative when the observations disagree
rationale: Trichome development and maturation can vary with plant age, genotype, and position, so representative sampling across the plant provides a stronger maturity assessment.
